label: Quasi-realism's answer to whether…, from Quasi-realism: moral sentences can be true… and 1 more
meaning: First verified entry of the quasi-realism deviation map (#185). Where quasi-realism (minimal, not robust, truth-aptness, SEP §1.1) holds and there is a moral sentence (Geach's, #182), its answer to Q-ROBUST-TRUTH is not equivalent to realism's (robust truth-aptness, SEP preamble). The corollary quasiRealistMapIsDistinctRival in the Solution puts this in answer-map terms: any maps giving these answer contents at some question that the quasi-realist map actually answers do not match there (a matching realist map would also have to answer), so quasi-realism escapes the collapse lemma through this deviation. Countermodels show both premises are needed. Scope: this establishes the deviation, not that quasi-realism is false. Why moral truth must be robust is the deviation target, which ties to Q-MORAL-GROUNDING; there is no refutes relation.
